label: Where BRender 1.4's Windows and Linux builds part once both use BRender 1.3.2's sine (local trace, 17 October 2026)

builds.windows: MSVC x64 Release, /fp:precise default, BrQsort = MSVC CRT qsort
builds.linux: WSL Ubuntu 24.04, gcc 13.3.0 -O3 -DNDEBUG (no -march, no FMA), BrQsort = glibc qsort

scene_traced: sphere-smooth (24-bit Gouraud); the lighting call counter runs across the scene list

chain.step: screen geometry (x, y, z, w, sx, sy, sz, u, v)
vertex red before scaling (comp[C_R]) at call 328

cause: core/v1db/prepmesh.c sums the face normals of each shared vertex in the order BrQsort leaves them; BRender 1.4's BrQsort (core/fw/brqsort.c) calls the C library qsort, which orders equal keys differently in the MSVC and glibc runtimes, so the float sums round differently in the last bit

experiment.change: BrQsort replaced by one stable merge sort in both builds, nothing else changed

period_match: with the platform qsort, the Windows frames of the three Gouraud scenes are byte for byte the period 1.3.2 frames (CI run of #56, parity-period); the period lit textured torus is drawn by a different kernel and is not comparable
does_not_prove: that either tie order is right; BRender 1.3.2 itself calls qsort on MSVC and its own quicksort elsewhere, so the period builds also depend on the runtime. The 1998 binaries' runtime qsort was not measured.
